articles.title: SHIP FRAMER SITES WITH ANY AI
articles.summary: Framer MCP connects ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or Grok to Framer. Ask your agent for a landing page, a new blog post or a full site, and it builds it on the canvas, fills your CMS and publishes it live on your domain. It isn't code, an export, or a mockup: it's a real, editable Framer site you can review and tweak before you ship. It works wherever your AI tool runs, even your phone, and setup takes a minute.

articles.title: XBOX REDESIGNS ITS PC APP AND EXPANDS ITS WEB REFRESH
articles.summary: The refreshed Xbox PC app reorganizes the library, adds friends to navigation, and widens search across games, add-ons, and people. On the web, a new Library tab combines cloud-playable owned games and Game Pass titles, joined by a desktop mode and five high-contrast options.

articles.title: APPLE TV GETS SIGN LANGUAGE INTERPRETATION, AND IT'S A HUGE ACCESSIBILITY WIN
articles.summary: Apple TV is introducing sign language interpretation for selected films and shows starting November 13, with American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) support. Viewers can activate interpretations through a dedicated playback button, identify compatible titles through visible labels, and discover them using natural-language search or a curated collection. Each interpretation is developed and tested with Deaf and native signers, offering an alternative to captions across Apple devices and supported third-party platforms.

articles.title: ADOBE'S GOOGLE PARTNERSHIP HINTS AT A RADICALLY DIFFERENT FUTURE FOR PHOTOSHOP
articles.summary: Adobe and Google DeepMind are exploring a customized AI image model that could enable near-real-time editing in Photoshop, allowing users to make changes through text prompts and switch between variations without interrupting their workflow. Adobe is also integrating its creative tools into Google's AI Mode in Search, potentially connecting inspiration and content creation without requiring users to open separate applications. Expanded Gemini and Gemini Enterprise integrations will support conversational image editing, design customization, and PDF workflows, although the new Photoshop capabilities remain experimental.

articles.title: COMPLEX ENTERPRISE UX AND UI AT SCALE: THE CASE FOR DESIGN INFRASTRUCTURE
articles.summary: Enterprises scaling UX and UI should stop asking which design tool to buy and ask what design infrastructure they need instead. Machine-readable components and tokens, open standards, and self-hosting connect design to code, repos, and CI, so one change propagates everywhere. Closed platforms, by contrast, carry per-seat costs, manual workarounds, and lock-in, which can force a full rebuild when switching vendors.

articles.title: I LET AI BUILD. I DON'T LET AI DECIDE
articles.summary: AI gets the building work — research, first drafts, prototypes, and repeat tasks — because each has a check outside itself that exposes errors within minutes. Deciding stays human: financial choices, sensitive data, psychological advice, and messages sent in one's name either lack that check or can't be undone. Three questions sort any task: name the guideline, check who wrote it, and find whose signature is on the result.

articles.title: WHERE THE DISABLED BUTTON GOT ITS RULE
articles.summary: The familiar convention of graying out unavailable controls traces back to Apple's Lisa interface guidelines from 1980, when dimmed menu items could still be selected even though they performed no action. By 1983, Apple had changed the rule so disabled commands could no longer be activated, a behavior later inherited by Macintosh interfaces and HTML's disabled attribute. Comparing eight modern design systems reveals how this convention creates accessibility problems, particularly when disabled buttons cannot receive keyboard focus or explain why an action is unavailable, making focusable alternatives such as aria-disabled useful.

articles.title: THE TEAMS BUILDING AI MAKE THEIR SLIDES WITH PITCH
articles.summary: Pitch is how AI leaders like Perplexity, Legora, and Synthesia create on-brand decks at scale. With Pitch, you can collaborate on fully editable presentations and unlock agentic workflows, like personalizing slides with CRM data and call notes.

articles.title: SCREEN RECORDING AS A PROMPT
articles.summary: Record your screen, draw or point at what matters, say the change. Drop the session into Cursor, Claude, or Codex — free, local by default, and no long prompt to write.

articles.summary: Submit any URL. Get back the full page content as clean, readable Markdown.

articles.title: THE CHAT APP FOR CONSTRUCTION SITES
articles.summary: BRCKS is the construction app for builders and trades: chat on site, and the diary, punch-list items, and photos file themselves.

articles.title: ON BORROWING APPLE'S TYPE SCALE
articles.summary: Apple's macOS and iOS type scales now drive a personal site's typography, with interface text at 13 on desktop and 17 on compact or touch layouts. Numbers outside a four-pixel grid are deliberate, since a spacing grid can't decide the relationship between kinds of text. Article bodies keep the larger 17 on desktop too, and a Dynamic Type fallback lets text scale with system settings on older iPhone and iPad browsers.

articles.title: KOTO POINTS GIFFGAFF TOWARD ITS NEXT CHAPTER WITH AN ARROW-LED REBRAND
articles.summary: Koto has refreshed UK telecom provider Giffgaff's identity around the idea of helping customers decide their next move, introducing an arrow integrated into the final letter of its wordmark. The arrow becomes a functional graphic device throughout the system, accompanied by acid green, a custom condensed typeface called Giffsans, and candid flash-lit photography that reinforces the brand's community-focused personality. Built on Giffgaff's existing design tokens, the identity extends across its website, app, packaging, and campaigns while preserving the challenger brand's recognizable character.

articles.title: HOW+HOW CREATES UNIFIED SUB-BRAND SYSTEM FOR PET RETAILER PETS
articles.summary: HOW+HOW has developed a connected brand architecture for UK pet retailer Pets, bringing its growing services together under a more coherent identity system. The project establishes distinct positioning, verbal identities, and visual systems for Pets Insurance, Pet Pals, and Pets Foundation, allowing each service to communicate its purpose while maintaining a connection to the parent brand. The approach addresses the fragmented nature of pet care, where retail, insurance, veterinary services, and guidance often operate independently, by creating a more recognizable ecosystem of related offerings.

articles.title: THIS BANK'S VIBRANT NEW LOGO DESIGN TICKS ALL THE BOXES
articles.summary: Brazilian state-owned bank Caixa Econômica Federal has unveiled its first major rebrand in 29 years.

articles.title: DIGITAL ARTIST MAX ASABIN USES EXPRESSIVE BRUSHWORK AND RADIANT SKIES TO CREATE ATMOSPHERIC FANTASY WORLDS
articles.summary: Max Asabin's painterly digital illustrations pair expressive brushwork and bold color with radiant sunset skies, from lone wanderers on grassy plains to twisted fantasy woodlands.

articles.title: THE ‘DUNE: PART 3' COSTUME DESIGNER EXPLAINS ITS GORGEOUS CLOTHES
articles.summary: Jacqueline West's costumes for Dune: Part Three go "more modern" and Renaissance-like, drawing on Goya, Balenciaga, Etruscan clothing, and early papal imagery.
